name: Heat Sink Sizing
blurb: required thermal resistance and heat sink size from power and ambient
intro: Works the series thermal path junction → case → sink → air backwards: the sink may have at most θSA = (Tj,max − margin − Ta)/P − θJC − θCS. The heat sink volume is estimated from typical volumetric thermal resistance for the chosen air flow (Aavid/Boyd design guidance).

inputs.label: Ambient (air at the sink)
inputs.help: Air inside an enclosure is often 10–20 °C above room.

inputs.label: Case to sink θCS
inputs.help: TO-220 size: grease 0.3–0.5, phase-change 0.3, silicone pad 1–2.5, mica + grease 1–1.5, dry 1–1.5. Scale by area for other packages.

inputs.label: Package θJA without sink (optional)
inputs.help: From the datasheet, e.g. TO-220 ≈ 62, TO-247 ≈ 40, DPAK on minimum pad ≈ 100. Leave empty to skip.

examples.title: Linear regulator in TO-220 burning 10 W, natural convection
TO-247 MOSFET, 35 W, fan at 2.5 m/s, insulating pad

usage: Give the dissipated power in W, ambient in °C, maximum junction and a design margin in °C, θJC and θCS in °C/W, the air flow (natural, 1, 2.5 or 5 m/s) and optionally the package's θJA without a sink. It returns the maximum sink-to-ambient θSA, the case and sink temperatures when the sink just meets it, an estimated heat sink volume range in cm³ and a table of typical heat sink classes that meet it. Use it before choosing a heat sink part; then check the chosen part's θSA curve at this power.
sources: Series thermal path Tj = Ta + P·(θJC + θCS + θSA) - e.g. Texas Instruments SPRA953 'Semiconductor and IC package thermal metrics'
Volumetric thermal resistance: natural 500–800, 1 m/s 150–250, 2.5 m/s 80–150, 5 m/s 50–80 cm³·°C/W - Aavid Thermalloy (Boyd) 'How to select a heat sink'
Heat sink class ranges in the table are a rule of thumb from catalogue data
